title: Ectopic pregnancy
what: The pregnancy has implanted outside the womb, most often in a tube. It cannot continue, and timely treatment is important: with medicine, an injection, or keyhole surgery.
why: When the pregnancy test is positive but the ultrasound shows no pregnancy in the womb, or with pain low on one side and spotting.
duration: laparoscopy usually takes 30 to 90 minutes, with 1 to 3 days in hospital; with an injection, blood tests for several weeks
tell_doctor: Your pain: where, since when, and if it spreads to the shoulder
Allergies, and heart, liver, or kidney conditions
A past ectopic pregnancy or belly surgery

prepare.title: Urgent
prepare.text: Treatment is often the same day. If the pain is severe or you feel dizzy, call emergency services right away.

prepare.title: Options
prepare.text: Early on, an injection of medicine sometimes works. If not, keyhole surgery. Your doctor will decide based on tests and ultrasound.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Do not eat or drink until your doctor decides. You may need anesthesia.

steps: The doctor does an ultrasound and takes blood for the pregnancy hormone
If an injection is chosen, it is given, and you then have blood tests a few times until the hormone drops
If surgery, you change, and a drip is placed
Under general anesthesia, the surgeon makes a few small cuts in your belly
The pregnancy is removed, sometimes with the tube
You wake up in the recovery room and are watched
feel: Pain at the small cuts. You will get painkillers
Shoulder pain from the gas is common and passes in 1 to 2 days
Sadness and worry are natural. You can ask for support
after: You can usually get up the same day or the next
No heavy lifting for a few weeks
Sometimes the pregnancy hormone is tested until it reaches zero, as your doctor plans
If you are Rh negative, you may need an anti-D injection
Talk to your doctor about future pregnancy and birth control
red_flags: Sudden belly pain, shoulder pain, dizziness, or fainting: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus at the small cuts

faq.a: No. It cannot grow outside the womb and is life-threatening. It must be treated.

faq.q: Will I be able to get pregnant later?
faq.a: Most women can, even with one tube. Your doctor will say when to plan.
From the gas used in laparoscopy, or from blood in the belly. If it hurts before surgery, call emergency services right away.
